public_surface_changed: type PackageReleaseVersion = { major: number; minor: number; patch: number }
@packmind/deployments: PackageReleaseSchema (via infra/schemas barrel and deploymentsSchemas array)

deviations.spec_said: Cover 'writes nothing when the release row and its joins cannot all be written' by driving createWithVersions with a non-existent version id and asserting no package_releases row was created; leave the case out and say so if pg-mem cannot support the assertion honestly.
deviations.did: Kept the case as 'when a pinned version does not exist > refuses the release', asserting only the rejection, with a comment in the spec explaining why the row-absence assertion is absent. createWithVersions still does all four inserts inside this.repository.manager.transaction(...).
deviations.why: pg-mem enforces the join-table foreign key (the write does reject), but its pg adapter treats ROLLBACK as a no-op - verified standalone: an insert inside BEGIN survives an explicit ROLLBACK, and the first run of the test showed the release row plus the command/standard join rows persisting. A 'leaves no release row behind' assertion could therefore never be honest in this harness.

deviations.spec_said: If this repository already has an established helper type for timestamp fields that sibling types use, prefer it over the two optional Date fields.
deviations.did: Kept the verbatim createdAt?: Date; updatedAt?: Date; fields.
deviations.why: No sibling type in packages/types/src/deployments uses WithTimestamps (Distribution and PackagesDeployment declare createdAt: string; the deployments schemas apply WithTimestamps at the EntitySchema level only). WithTimestamps would also make createdAt/updatedAt required on the createWithVersions input, forcing callers to invent DB-generated values.

notes: 13 tests pass; lint+typecheck clean for deployments, types, migrations. No `package` many-to-one on the schema, so the package_id FK lives in the migration only. Pre-existing, untouched: DistributedPackageSchema's joinTable name disagrees with migration 1764700000000.
26 tests pass; lint and typecheck clean. Test fixtures use `as unknown as string` casts to turn branded ids into the plain strings the snapshot type takes, rather than widening with `any`.

behaviour_delta: A package release can be cut through the deployments port. An empty package is refused with no_components before the version is validated; the current version is the greatest release by parsed triple, or 0.0.0. A 23505 on insert becomes not_greater carrying the re-read version.
notes: 17 tests pass; lint (0 errors) and typecheck clean for deployments and types. PackageReleaseService exposes listReleases/findByVersion beyond createRelease so the later readiness unit has a seam.

Characterization refactor: the 17 CreatePackageReleaseUseCase tests pass unmodified. Attempt 1 gated FAIL scope only because the executor committed its own work, leaving a clean tree; soft-reset and re-gated. Not a boundary violation.

behaviour_delta: One member read returns a package's releases newest first by parsed triple plus readiness: currentVersion (null when unreleased), verdict, the three offerable versions, and the pinned components behind their latest version.
notes: Pre-existing no-non-null-assertion lint warnings in deployments repositories were left untouched.

blocked.question: Soft-deleted CommandVersion and StandardVersion rows are absent from the hydrated relations despite withDeleted(). Is this a pg-mem limitation that makes the assertions vacuous, or a real defect?
options_considered: Record AC-18 as untestable in this harness, as D-027 and D-028 do for genuine pg-mem limits
Weaken the assertion to something that passes

notes: Blocked correctly, diagnosed wrongly. The tests are right; the empty arrays are a real defect, not a harness limit. Diagnosis in D-038. Resolved by widening scope to the repository in attempt 2.

behaviour_delta: A release now shows the versions it pinned even after those versions are soft-deleted.
notes: 16 tests, 0 lint errors. Three attempts: blocked on a real defect, fixed the withDeleted() ordering, then cleared an unused binding left by attempt 1.

behaviour_delta: Clients can read a single package release by version, receiving all pinned component versions including those whose components have since been deleted.
notes: 5 tests, 0 lint errors. Attempt 1 gated FAIL scope on the orchestrator's own charter.md edit, which alwaysInScope does not cover; committed separately and re-gated.

Fixture promotion: command, standard and skill moved from consts inside beforeAll to outer-scope lets, so the new block can insert a newer version row for the same component. 20 PackageReleaseRepository tests pass, 16 existing plus 4 new.

behaviour_delta: A caller can list a package's releases with the panel's readiness, cut a release by POSTing {version}, and read one release by version including components deleted since. A refused cut answers 400 with {code, currentVersion}, not prose; a missing package or version answers 404.

deviations.spec_said: Cover six listed cases in the spec.
deviations.did: Wrote nine it blocks: the six required, plus two passthrough assertions split from the delegation ones, plus PackageNotFoundError -> NotFoundException on the listing route.
deviations.why: Same coverage, finer failure attribution; every it name contains 'release' so the exit criterion still selects them all.

notes: 9 passed; lint and typecheck clean for api. Unrelated, not fixed: PackageNotFoundError calls Object.setPrototypeOf, which this repo's TypeScript standard forbids; getPackageSummaryBySlug still maps 404 by string-matching the message.
index.ts re-exports PackageRelease.ts with `export *`, so it needed no edit. nx typecheck api and the api controller spec also pass: no consumer reads createdAt or updatedAt off a release response.

behaviour_delta: Frontend can now call the three package-release HTTP endpoints (list, create, get) through typed gateway methods with React Query hooks. The create mutation invalidates only the list-releases key for the specific package (D-016).
